newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PICK 'N PAY BLASTS S.AFRICAN DRINK LAWS.
newsitem.headline: PICK 'N PAY BLASTS S.AFRICAN DRINK LAWS.

text.p: Retail group Pick 'n Pay Holdings Ltd on Tuesday blasted South Africa's drink laws saying the legislation governing the sale of alcoholic drink was outdated and unconstitutional.
Pick 'n Pay group enterprises managing director Gareth Ackerman said the prohibition on selling alcohol on Sundays on religous grounds ignored the multi-cultural nature of South Africa.
"The insistence on Sunday as a holy day ignores the fact that many South Africans celebrate their holy day on other days of the week," Ackerman said.

He said South Africa's new consitution, signed into law on Tuesday, prohibits any form of religious discrimination. "It is our contention that restrictions forbidding the sale of liqour on Sundays contravenes the provisions of the new constitution," he added.
Ackerman said many people -- especially overseas tourists -- were against the laws and shopkeepers often flouted them.
"In the face of growing consumer demand, many small grocers are simply breaking the law, in the hope that they won't be caught," he said.
Ackerman said the drink laws should be reformed along the lines of moves that have relaxed rules governing comercial trading, sport and cinema opening on Sundays.
